I proposed these from the 100 experiments plus general reasoning about the cell. Each hypothesis rests on only a few parent cells, so none is strongly established.

1. Replacing an empty edge 3 with a convolution adds a new input-to-output path, so the gain is larger than when it replaces an existing operation (items 71 vs 72–74).
2. The same holds for `skip_connect` on edge 3 (items 21 vs 22–24).
3. Removing edge 0 hurts much more when edge 1 is `none`, because that can disconnect the input (item 65).
4. The same applies when edge 5 is `none` (item 69).
5. The same applies when edge 3 is `none` (item 67).
6. Setting edge 5 to `skip_connect` is better when the direct 0→3 path is missing, since it supplies a shortcut (items 85 vs 83 and 86).
7. Setting edge 4 to a 3x3 conv gains less when edge 0 is `none`, because the node 1 input is cut off (items 55 and 56 vs 52–54).
8. Setting edge 2 to `avg_pool_3x3` is much worse in the all-skip or pooling-heavy cells (items 95, 96 and 98), where it destroys the only conv path.
9. Edge 0 → 3x3 helps less when edge 0 was already a 1x1 conv, since the upgrade is smaller than from `none` or `skip_connect` (item 3 vs 1, 2 and 5).
10. Edge 0 → 3x3 is slightly worse when edge 3 is `none` (item 8, the only negative one), because a direct bypass is missing.
